summary: This paper provides a definitive resolution to the open analytic, combinatorial, and arithmetic structure of Huffman sequence distance geometry recently posed by Huggins, Şahin, and Erkip (2026). Replacing finite-point Parseval DFT sums with unit-circle Cauchy residue calculus and cyclotomic Galois theory, the author establishes four major theorems: (1) an exact closed-form dipole law and universal O(1/K) minimax ceiling with a sharp K=16 phase transition refuting the even-K crossover conjecture; (2) universal uniform-sign Hamming-weight collapse; (3) a complete odd-K arithmetic dichotomy via cyclotomic polynomials; and (4) unconditional global minimax optimality for K=2,3,4. The theoretical results are backed by an exceptionally rigorous formalization scope comprising 20 Lean 4.36.0 proofs, 16 exact rational/cyclotomic SHA-256 certificates, and 69 adversarial tests.
strengths: Complete resolution of all open conjectures and large-R asymptotic behaviors from Huggins et al. (2026).
Exemplary double-layer formal verification combining pure Lean 4 core proofs (zero sorry) and exact-Q Python cyclotomic certificates.
Elegant application of Cauchy residue calculus on |z|=1 and cyclotomic Galois theory over Q.

weaknesses: The exposition is dense and algebraically heavy, which is inherent to the complexity of the domain but demands careful reading.
Results focus strictly on Huffman sequence Euclidean distance barriers, leaving broader sequence design generalizations for future work.
